content: {"rule": "K-C", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge text decides the D5 vs C5 link collision by assessing whether CR2 G answers particular rows and leaves the sign's sense open, which is the chain-against-chain setting the rule governs.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] G answers the 'almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows, leaving the sign's sense open.", "rule_words": "When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.", "room": "weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse: either the judge must assess the whole chain's support, or it may still rule underdetermined because individual rows leave the sense open; I weighed the former.", "why": "The judge text treats the collision as underdetermined because named rows leave the sign's sense open, which is row-by-row analysis rather than the required chain-against-chain footing."}
